RetroWP — third-party components in this binary
===============================================

RetroWP is Copyright the RetroWP authors and licensed GPL-2.0-or-later.
The full licence text accompanies this file as COPYING.

This binary also contains, or is built from, the following:


retroplat — the platform seam
-----------------------------
LGPL-2.1-or-later.  Source: https://github.com/slaapliedje/retroplat

Under section 6 of that licence you are entitled to modify retroplat and
relink this program against your modified copy.  RetroWP's own source is
published in full (https://github.com/slaapliedje/retrowp), and building
it against a modified retroplat needs no more than:

    make RETROPLAT=/path/to/your/retroplat

The build requirements for each target are in that repository's README.


gem4xe application kit — Atari 8-bit builds only
------------------------------------------------
The kit compiled into a .G4A carries gem4xe's terms, and WHICH terms
depends on when the binary was built: GPLv2-or-later up to and including
kit 0.4, LGPL-2.1-or-later from gem4xe's 2026-09-28 relicence onward.
The build that produced this archive records its kit in
docs/gem4xe-port.md.  Source: https://github.com/slaapliedje/gem4xe


Calypsi compiler runtime — Atari 8-bit builds only
--------------------------------------------------
A .G4A links a small amount of compiler support code from Calypsi's
runtime archive (pseudoRegisters.o, integer.o, memory.o, controlFlow.o,
spill.o, initialize.o, vswitch16.o, vswitch32.o).  A compiler's runtime,
shipped with the compiler and linked into every program it produces, is
a "System Library" as the GPL uses that term -- GPLv3 section 1 names "a
compiler used to produce the work", and GPLv2 section 3 carries the
older form of the same exception.

Two of those objects (memcpy_far, memset_far, where linked) are NuttX's
under the three-clause BSD licence, Copyright (C) 2007, 2011 Gregory
Nutt.  Its second clause asks that the notice travel with binary
distributions, which is the purpose of this paragraph.

Calypsi's Apache-2.0 C library is NOT linked: gem4xe supplies its own
string and memory functions so that no Apache-2.0 object code enters a
GPL binary.


MiNTLib — Atari ST builds only
------------------------------
This program uses MiNTLib (https://github.com/freemint/mintlib).  Most
of MiNTLib is under COPYMINT, a permissive licence whose "credits"
clause asks that any program using the code say so in its
documentation; this paragraph is that acknowledgement.  Other parts of
MiNTLib are GPLv2.  Both are compatible with this program's own licence.


Toolchain runtimes on the other targets
---------------------------------------
Each backend links its own toolchain's C runtime, and a compiler's
runtime -- shipped with the compiler, linked into every program it
produces -- is a "System Library" as the GPL uses that term.

  Atari ST   MiNTLib 0.60.1 (above), and gemlib, whose distribution
             states no licence at all -- an open question, recorded
             rather than assumed either way.
  DOS        Open Watcom, under the Sybase Open Watcom Public License
             1.0.  GPLv3's System Library wording covers a statically
             linked compiler runtime plainly, which is part of why this
             program is "or later" rather than GPLv2 alone.
  Amiga      libnix, which likewise states no licence in its
             distribution.
  Mac        Retro68, not audited: its toolchain does not currently
             build here, so no Mac binary is produced.

All GCC-based targets also link libgcc, which carries the GCC Runtime
Library Exception.
